I had to remove the caliper to change orings so in my case the caliper was not connected to the hyd line. But I think it could be done with it connected and no bleeding required. answer:
A few practical approaches from Cozy builders:

- **Try reverse bleeding:** push clean fluid in through the caliper bleeder and up toward the master-cylinder reservoir. Builders report this can move stubborn air out effectively, though it takes a suitable setup. [1][2] Watch the reservoir closely so it doesn’t overflow.
- **Use clear tubing** at the bleed point so you can see whether bubbles are still coming through. Air can also hang up at high points in the plumbing; one builder added bleedable connections at those points. [13]
- **Check caliper orientation and line routing.** The discussions don’t establish a universal minimum mounting angle for bleeding; reported installations vary, and the right orientation depends on the caliper’s internal passages and how you’re bleeding it. For your W51LXT, ask Matco for its recommended orientation rather than relying on a general angle rule. [1][11]
- **Use the specified fluid.** Matco recommends MIL-H-5606 or compatible fluid; DOT 5 may be used, but DOT 5.1, DOT 3, and DOT 4 should not be used in these setups. [2] If the system has had the wrong fluid in it, check with Matco about flushing and seal replacement. [6]
- If the pedal is still soft after you’re no longer seeing bubbles, check for leaks and confirm the master-cylinder setup as well as the bleeding. Matco’s recommended pedal mechanical advantage is 2.5:1. [9]
